newsitem.title: USA: Oscar Mayer to sponsor Super Bowl halftime show.
newsitem.headline: Oscar Mayer to sponsor Super Bowl halftime show.

text.p: Oscar Mayer, whose cold cuts are featured at many a Super Bowl party, said Thursday that it will sponsor the halftime show for the National Football League's championship game for the second time in January.

As part of the multimillion dollar package, the Madison, Wis.-based maker of cold cuts, hot dogs, bacon and pickles, said it also has renewed its team sponsorship deal with the NFL for the fall of 1997.
"This is the second year in a row that we've sponsored the Super Bowl Halftime Show," Steve Shanesy, Oscar Mayer vice president of marketing, said in an interview.
"We saw tremendous business results behind our Super Bowl sponsorship and our Super Bowl promotions," he said.

While Shanesy would not give the exact value of the deal, advertising time for the Super Bowl this year is expected to sell at around last year's price of $1.2 million to $1.3 million for a 30-second spot.
The game at the end of the current season will be broadcast for the first time by Fox Television, a unit of News Corp. Ltd.
Shanesy said the game offers advertisers a unique showcase, and added that for viewers the food at their Super Bowl parties is almost as important as the game itself.
"The Super Bowl is the biggest party day of the year," he said. The game is also a showcase for advertisers who use the huge audience to kick off their campaigns for the year.

"We saw the biggest single jump in our advertising awareness that we've ever had from our Super Bowl advertising," he said. "Everyone often looks with as much interest at what new commercials are going to be unveiled" as at the game itself.

Besides having the halftime show named for Oscar Mayer, the deal includes a 60-second spot during halftime, two 10-second promotional spots in the first half of the game, as well as a five second lead-in to the halftime show and a five second trailer at the end.
Shanesy said the halftime show itself was in the planning stages. The game is to be played on January 26 at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans.

Oscar Mayer, a subsidiary of the Kraft Foods unit of Philip Morris Cos. Inc., also will be a sponsor of the NFL Experience, the league's theme park set up each year at the game. Shanesy said among other activities, the company's famous hot-dog-shaped Wienermobile will be there.
